item.title: Echizen Washi Village: 1,500 Years of Japanese Papermaking — Guide
item.description: Echizen has produced washi (traditional Japanese paper) for around 1,500 years, making it one of Japan’s foremost and oldest papermaking regions, historically prized for high-quality paper used in everything from official documents to art and calligraphy. The Echizen Washi Village gathers the craft’s heritage in one area, with a paper museum, a preserved historic papermaking house and workshops where visitors can try hands-on paper-making themselves, dipping and forming a sheet of washi to take home as a souvenir.
